# Build a stronger CV in minutes with AI

**Hook:**
You’ll walk away able to turn a messy list of jobs into a clear, professional CV and tweak it for each role in under 20 minutes. No design skills required.

## Before you start
- A free AI chat tool (we’ll use **ChatGPT**, **Gemini**, or **Claude**)
- Your work history in a simple list (job titles, dates, key tasks)
- One job description you’d like to target

---

## Step 1 — Gather your raw material
Open your notes or a blank page and write every job you’ve ever had in one short line each. Include the dates and 2–3 bullet points of what you did.

💬 Example:
```
2022–2024  Café Manager, Brew House
- Led a team of 8 during peak hours
- Created weekly rosters and handled payroll
- Reduced waste by 15 % through better ordering
```

## Step 2 — Paste into an AI chat and ask for a first draft
Open your chosen AI chat (ChatGPT, Gemini, or Claude). Paste your raw list and add this prompt:

> “Turn the list below into a clean, professional CV in Australian English. Use a simple reverse-chronological layout. Keep it to one page. Use bullet points, not paragraphs. Do not add any made-up details.”

💬 Example prompt you can copy:
```
List:
2022–2024  Café Manager, Brew House
- Led a team of 8 during peak hours
- Created weekly rosters and handled payroll
- Reduced waste by 15 % through better ordering

Turn the list into a clean, professional CV in Australian English.
Use a simple reverse-chronological layout.
Keep it to one page.
Use bullet points, not paragraphs.
Do not add any made-up details.
```

## Step 3 — Polish the language
Ask the AI to make the bullet points stronger and more active. Use:

> “Rewrite every bullet point to start with a strong action verb and include a quantifiable result where possible.”

💬 Example you can paste:
```
Rewrite every bullet point to start with a strong action verb and include a quantifiable result where possible.
```

## Step 4 — Tailor for the job you want
Copy the job description you’re targeting. Ask the AI:

> “Rewrite my CV bullet points so they match the keywords and skills in this job description: [paste description].”

💬 Example:
```
Job description snippet:
"Seeking a café manager who can lead teams, manage rosters, and reduce food waste."

Rewrite my CV bullet points to match those keywords.
```

## Step 5 — Format and export
Ask the AI to give you plain text you can copy into any word processor:

> “Give me the final CV in plain text so I can copy it into Word or Google Docs.”

💬 Example:
```
Give me the final CV in plain text so I can copy it into Word or Google Docs.
```

---

## Common mistakes
- **Over-editing**: Don’t change every word; let the AI do the heavy lifting and only tweak what feels off.
- **Adding fluff**: Never let the AI invent a degree, award, or skill you don’t have.
- **Ignoring keywords**: Always paste the job description so the AI can mirror its language.

---

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life**: Update your CV once, then reuse it for every application by swapping in the right keywords.
- **For your business or work**: Keep a master CV in plain text and ask the AI to tailor it to each client proposal or tender.
- **If you're just getting started**: Start with your most recent job and build one page at a time.

---

## Try it now
Open your chosen AI chat, paste the example prompt from Step 2, and hit send. You’ll have a first draft in under two minutes.
